title: Liaodong
capsule: Liaodong (遼東) was one of the Eighteen Kingdoms Xiang Yu created in 206 BCE from the former state of Yan, assigned to Han Guang — the deposed King of Yan — as a territory in southern Liaoning centred on the old commandery seat of Xiangping (modern Liaoyang). Han Guang, resentful of his demotion, refused to relocate and remained at Wuzhong, where his own former general Zang Tu — who had been made King of Yan proper — attacked and killed him within a year of the settlement (206–205 BCE), annexing Liaodong into a reunified Yan. Liaodong's independent existence therefore lasted only about a year.
